risk_types.name: Unlimited liability
risk_types.definition: A party's liability is uncapped, excluded from any limitation, or expressly unlimited.

template.title: Unlimited liability clause
template.explanation: The clause removes any cap on what a party may have to pay for losses under the contract.
template.reason: Uncapped liability exposes the liable party to losses far larger than the contract value.
template.improvement: Negotiate an aggregate liability cap (for example, 12 months of fees) with narrow carve-outs such as fraud.

risk_types.name: High penalty clauses
risk_types.definition: Penalties, liquidated damages or service credits that are large relative to the contract value or the breach.

template.title: High penalty or liquidated damages
template.explanation: The clause sets a penalty or pre-agreed damages payable on breach or delay.
template.reason: Large fixed penalties can exceed the real loss and create disproportionate financial exposure.
template.improvement: Cap penalties at a reasonable percentage of the affected fees and make them the sole remedy for that breach.

risk_types.name: Automatic payment obligations
risk_types.definition: Payments are charged, debited or invoiced automatically without approval or notice.

template.title: Automatic payment obligation
template.explanation: Payments are taken or invoiced automatically under this clause.
template.reason: Automatic charges reduce control over spend and make disputed amounts harder to withhold.
template.improvement: Require prior written approval or a notice period before any automatic charge, and a right to dispute it.

risk_types.name: Late payment penalties
risk_types.definition: Interest, fees or suspension rights triggered by late payment.

template.title: Late payment penalty
template.explanation: The clause charges interest or fees, or allows suspension, when payment is late.
template.reason: High late-payment interest or quick suspension can escalate costs during genuine invoice disputes.
template.improvement: Limit interest to a statutory or modest rate, add a grace period, and exclude amounts disputed in good faith.

risk_types.name: Hidden charges
risk_types.definition: Fees, surcharges or price increases that are not fixed in the pricing schedule or can be changed unilaterally.
queries: reserves the right to change fees

template.title: Charges that are not fixed
template.explanation: The clause allows extra fees or price changes outside the agreed pricing.
template.reason: Unfixed or unilateral charges make the true cost of the contract unpredictable.
template.improvement: List all fees in the pricing schedule, cap annual increases, and require written agreement for new charges.

risk_types.name: Missing confidentiality
risk_types.definition: No clause protects confidential information exchanged under the contract.

template.title: No confidentiality clause
template.explanation: The contract does not contain a clause protecting confidential information.
template.reason: Without confidentiality terms, sensitive business information shared under the contract is not protected.
template.improvement: Add mutual confidentiality obligations with a defined term, permitted disclosures and return or destruction of information.

risk_types.name: Missing governing law
risk_types.definition: The contract does not state which law governs it, or states it unclearly.

template.title: Governing law not specified
template.explanation: The contract does not state which country's or state's law applies.
template.reason: Without governing law, disputes start with an argument about which law applies, adding cost and uncertainty.
template.improvement: Add a governing-law clause naming a specific jurisdiction.

risk_types.name: Missing jurisdiction
risk_types.definition: The contract does not say which courts or arbitration forum resolve disputes.

template.title: Jurisdiction not specified
template.explanation: The contract does not name the courts or arbitration forum for disputes.
template.reason: Without a forum, either party may sue in an inconvenient or unfavourable location.
template.improvement: Add a jurisdiction or arbitration clause naming the forum, seat and language.

risk_types.name: Missing termination rights
risk_types.definition: No clause allows the parties to terminate for breach, convenience or insolvency.

template.title: No termination rights
template.explanation: The contract does not set out when or how a party may terminate it.
template.reason: Without termination rights, a party may be locked in even after serious breach.
template.improvement: Add termination for material breach (with a cure period), insolvency and, where possible, convenience.

risk_types.name: Ambiguous language
risk_types.definition: Key terms are left to be agreed later, undefined, or open to one party's interpretation.
patterns: to be (mutually )?(agreed|determined|confirmed|decided)( upon)?( later| at a later date| in due course| separately)?

template.title: Ambiguous or open-ended wording
template.explanation: The clause leaves an important term undefined or to be agreed later.
template.reason: Open-ended terms are a common source of disputes because each party can read them differently.
template.improvement: Replace open-ended wording with specific, measurable terms or a defined mechanism for deciding them.

risk_types.name: Automatic renewal
risk_types.definition: The contract renews automatically unless a party gives notice.

template.title: Automatic renewal
template.explanation: The contract renews for a further term unless a party cancels in time.
template.reason: Missing the cancellation window commits the party to another full term and its costs.
template.improvement: Require written reminder before renewal, shorten the non-renewal notice window, or make renewal opt-in.

risk_types.name: Vendor lock-in
risk_types.definition: Terms that make switching provider costly: exclusivity of supply, proprietary formats, no exit assistance, minimum commitments or exit fees.

template.title: Vendor lock-in
template.explanation: The clause makes it costly or difficult to move to another provider.
template.reason: Lock-in weakens negotiating position at renewal and raises the cost of exit.
template.improvement: Add exit assistance, data export in a standard format, and remove or reduce exit fees and minimum commitments.

risk_types.name: Long notice period
risk_types.definition: A notice period for termination or non-renewal longer than the configured threshold.

template.title: Long notice period
template.explanation: The clause requires a long notice period before termination or non-renewal.
template.reason: Long notice periods delay exit and extend payment obligations after a decision to leave.
template.improvement: Reduce the notice period to 30–60 days, or make it mutual and proportionate to the contract term.

risk_types.name: One-sided obligations
risk_types.definition: Rights or discretions granted to one party only, without an equivalent for the other.
queries: may at any time without cause

template.title: One-sided right or obligation
template.explanation: The clause gives one party a right or discretion that the other party does not have.
template.reason: Unbalanced terms shift risk and control to one side and weaken the other party's remedies.
template.improvement: Make the right mutual, add objective criteria or notice, or require consent not to be unreasonably withheld.

risk_types.name: Exclusive agreements
risk_types.definition: Exclusivity, non-compete or non-solicitation restrictions on a party.

template.title: Exclusivity or non-compete restriction
template.explanation: The clause restricts a party from working with others or competing.
template.reason: Exclusivity limits commercial options and may be costly if the counterparty underperforms.
template.improvement: Limit exclusivity by scope, territory and duration, and tie it to performance targets.

risk_types.name: Missing GDPR clause
risk_types.definition: Personal data is processed but the contract does not address GDPR obligations.

template.title: No GDPR clause
template.explanation: The contract involves personal data but does not refer to GDPR obligations.
template.reason: Processing EU personal data without GDPR terms (Article 28) can lead to regulatory fines.
template.improvement: Add GDPR-compliant processing terms or attach a data processing agreement.

risk_types.name: Missing data protection clause
risk_types.definition: Personal data is processed but there are no data protection obligations.

template.title: No data protection clause
template.explanation: The contract involves personal data but sets no data protection obligations.
template.reason: Without data protection terms, responsibility for breaches and regulatory compliance is unclear.
template.improvement: Add data protection obligations: lawful processing, breach notification, sub-processor controls, deletion on exit.

risk_types.name: Missing security requirements
risk_types.definition: No information security obligations or standards.

template.title: No security requirements
template.explanation: The contract does not set information security obligations or standards.
template.reason: Without security terms, there is no contractual baseline to enforce if systems or data are compromised.
template.improvement: Add minimum security controls or a recognised standard (for example ISO 27001) and breach notification duties.

risk_types.name: Missing audit rights
risk_types.definition: No right to audit or inspect the other party's records or compliance.

template.title: No audit rights
template.explanation: The contract gives no right to audit or inspect the other party's records or compliance.
template.reason: Without audit rights, compliance with pricing, security and data obligations cannot be verified.
template.improvement: Add a right to audit on reasonable notice, at least annually and after any incident.

risk_types.name: Undefined deliverables
risk_types.definition: The services or deliverables are not described, or are left to be defined later.
queries: scope of services statement of work
patterns: deliverables?[^.]{0,40}(to be|shall be|will be) (agreed|determined|defined)( later| separately| in due course)

template.title: Deliverables not defined
template.explanation: The contract does not clearly define what must be delivered.
template.reason: Undefined deliverables make it impossible to prove non-performance or reject poor work.
template.improvement: Attach a statement of work listing each deliverable, its specification and due date.

risk_types.name: Undefined responsibilities
risk_types.definition: Who does what is left vague or to be agreed later.

template.title: Responsibilities not defined
template.explanation: The clause leaves the split of responsibilities vague or to be agreed later.
template.reason: Unclear responsibilities lead to gaps in delivery and disputes about who is at fault.
template.improvement: Add a responsibilities matrix (RACI) or list each party's obligations explicitly.

risk_types.name: Missing SLA
risk_types.definition: No service levels, availability targets or response times.

template.title: No service levels
template.explanation: The contract sets no service levels, availability targets or response times.
template.reason: Without SLAs there is no objective measure of performance and no remedy for poor service.
template.improvement: Add measurable service levels with reporting and service credits for missed targets.

risk_types.name: Missing acceptance criteria
risk_types.definition: No process or criteria for accepting or rejecting deliverables.

template.title: No acceptance criteria
template.explanation: The contract does not define how deliverables are tested and accepted.
template.reason: Without acceptance criteria, payment may fall due for work that does not meet requirements.
template.improvement: Add acceptance tests, a review period, a rejection process and a limit on deemed acceptance.
